articles.title_orig: Why Australia chose the world's biggest political stage to reveal OpenAI hack
articles.title_zh: Why Australia chose the world's biggest political stage to reveal OpenAI hack
articles.content_orig:
Australia made a dramatic revelation on Wednesday during the United Nations General Assembly.
Rogue AI agents had hacked one of its government bodies - the first known incident of its kind in the world. Private data, but not sensitive information, was taken from Medicare, Australia's universal healthcare scheme.
The breach happened in June, but OpenAI says it only became aware of it in August - and then took until 10 September to alert Australia's government, by sending an email to an address used by researchers and academics to alert authorities to concerns of vulnerabilities.
While worrying, the timing of the incident is somewhat of a gift for Australia.
A middle power that doesn't usually get as much of a platform as its influential allies, the country wants to be seen as punching above its weight on one of the most defining issues of our time - big tech regulation.
In the past year alone, it has implemented the world's strictest social media ban , announced what it says are the world's strongest algorithm controls , floated the possibility of "world-leading" limits on smart glasses , and is now the first government to confront AI firms over a rogue attack on its data.
It's entirely possible other governments have been the victim of rogue AI agents.
Former Australian government cybersecurity adviser Alastair MacGibbon told the BBC he'd heard whispers that several others have been notified of similar recent breaches by OpenAI agents.
"Some have chosen to not be public – that's every government's choice on how it wants to handle these things," the CyberCX chief strategy officer said. "The [Australian] government chose a time to release this to gain maximum publicity which is their wont to do."
Revealing a data breach can of course be a risky strategy for governments - it leaves them vulnerable to criticism that their security systems aren't up to scratch. But the fact that no sensitive information was leaked put Australia in a stronger position to use the incident.
"Nobody has died," says the University of Queensland's associate professor Michael Noetel, who studies AI risks. "This is another canary in the coal mine. This sort of loss-of-control incident, even though it's minor now, is what CEOs are worried about getting worse over time."
Though Australia has made a name for itself by taking a stand against social media companies, taking up the AI mantle now is another way for Australia to rein in big tech, says Tama Leaver, professor of internet studies at Curtin University in Perth.
"It's impossible to say for sure, but it seems incredibly likely that this was very carefully planned."
The fact that leaders were all together in New York this week has probably helped.
Albanese says he had a "frank" discussion with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express Australia's "extreme concern" about what happened. Altman acknowledged "issues with protocols" at OpenAI, he said.
The Australian leader also posed with Donald Trump for a selfie - and the two may have had face-to-face talks. But Australia risks the ire of the US president, who wants to encourage AI, "not rein it in", and even rename it "super intelligence" .
Earlier this week, the Albanese had to deflect criticism from the Trump administration over his government's proposal to give users the ability to opt out of social media algorithms. The US said it amounted to "censorship of protected speech".
Back home, Australia's very own eSafety commission is currently arming itself with lawyers, preparing to take on social media platforms objecting to its social media law for under 16s.
Australia isn't popular with big tech. But its bold policies on social media and internet safety have been largely supported among Australians themselves, especially parents.
The government is taking advantage of the hack to position itself as a leader on one of the biggest talking points of our time. And it's wasting no time in using the incident to advance the country's broader crusade.
Within hours of the announcement, Communications Minister Anika Wells told reporters: "This is an example of an unregulated industry where big tech clearly feels like they can do whatever they like, and that's not going to wash here in Australia."

articles.title_orig: Rapper Macklemore announces 'Free Palestine' tour after Ed Sheeran fallout
articles.title_zh: Rapper Macklemore announces 'Free Palestine' tour after Ed Sheeran fallout
articles.content_orig:
Rapper Macklemore is launching a "Free Palestine" tour, days after being dropped from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour following pro-Palestinian comments he made  onstage earlier this month.
"So, as you all know, my schedule freed up a bit," he said upon announcing the tour on Thursday.
The American artist - whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty - said proceeds from the tour, which launches in Dublin next month, will go to organisations supporting Palestinians.
Macklemore's onstage comments and subsequent removal from the tour led Sheeran's support acts to drop out, while the British singer stressed that the decision to drop the rapper was made by his promoter, not by himself.
In a statement on Thursday, the rapper said that the last couple of weeks had shown him there had been "a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now".
"What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," he said. "When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."
Macklemore said he had spent the last week contacting artists who had used their platforms to stand in solidarity with the Palestinian people, regardless of the consequences.
Due to how quickly the tour came together, several details were still being worked out, he added: "But this is a moment of momentum, and there is work to be done."
Macklemore's new tour will begin in Dublin on 26 October followed by Paris on 29 October and London on 30 October.
US dates will also be added, he said, with additional tickets going on sale next week.
While performing as the opening act for Sheeran at a concert in early September in New Jersey, Macklemore said: "A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine."
The Thrift Shop rapper then performed a song dedicated to pro-Palestinian protesters at Columbia University.
After he was taken off the tour on 14 September, Macklemore accused stadium owners of rallying together to push him out. He was also accused by billionaire stadium owner Robert Kraft of hate speech and antisemitic rhetoric surrounding Israel and Gaza.
Sheeran early on said that the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour was made by concert promoter Messina Touring Group.
His early remarks led to all of his support acts to drop out of the tour in solidarity, and fans to express frustration. Ticket prices for the tour plummeted as well.
Sheeran addressed the controversy head-on during the start of his set in Philadelphia last week.
He said he had made "mistakes" handling the fallout, apologising to fans and taking a stand on the Israel-Gaza conflict, which he said was "a humanitarian issue".
He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as "horrific", and also called the situation in Gaza "unjustifiable and disproportionate".

articles.title_orig: All-WNBA First and Second Teams: SB Nation’s official picks
articles.title_zh: All-WNBA First and Second Teams: SB Nation’s official picks
articles.content_orig:
A’ja Wilson, Olivia Miles, and Caitlin Clark headline my All-WNBA First Team. Here are my full picks and rationale.
It’s time for one of my most difficult WNBA end-of-season award decisions: the dreaded All-WNBA First and Second Teams.
I’ll start by sharing my general philosophy in selecting players for the All-WNBA First and Second Teams. When it comes to this award (and, to be frank, most others), I strongly value winning and generally believe all of the top-performing teams should be sufficiently represented. As such, I aimed to have at least one player from each of the 8 playoff teams on the All-WNBA team.
That meant that players who had individually strong seasons — like Toronto Tempo guard Marina Mabrey, Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas, and Mercury guard Kahleah Copper — began my calculus at a strong disadvantage. These players would have had to have otherworldly seasons to be considered, not just strong ones.
I’ll dive into my rationale in a moment, but first, here are my official selections:
Ultimately, Olivia Miles and A’ja Wilson were both First Team no-brainers. Miles has been the best player on the WNBA’s best team; Wilson has been the MVP (and the league’s leading scorer and shot-blocker). Not much more needs to be said there.
Breanna Stewart and Paige Bueckers have been the best players on lower-ranked playoff teams, which, in theory, should not guarantee them a spot on First Team All-WNBA. But both players have shouldered massive loads (on both ends, really) and are far and away the biggest reasons why their teams are in the playoffs. While teams like the Mystics, the Dream, and the Fever have two or three players who shoulder substantial and somewhat similar responsibilities, when it comes to the Liberty and the Wings, there is no question around who their undisputed MVP is. And both players’ on-court production speaks for itself; Bueckers has been the WNBA’s 5th-leading scorer; Stewart has been the 7th.
I really struggled with the fact that Kelsey Mitchell was on the All-WNBA Second Team considering the incredible scoring year she’s had. But it was between her and Caitlin Clark for First Team, because the Fever’s record did not justify having two First Team players. Ultimately, Mitchell has had the more impressive pure scoring season, but Clark has been the league’s third-leading scorer and best playmaker, and shoulders more offensive responsibilities. As such, she secured a spot on First Team.
I also had to grapple with the fact that the Valkyries did not have a First Team All-WNBA player when they have been the second-best record in the WNBA. But I voted Natalie Nakase for Coach of the Year, and picked three Valkyries players for First Team All-Defense, so Golden State was well-represented in other sections of my ballot.
When it came to Second Team, there was no doubt Kelsey Mitchell was going to be included after her omission from my First Team. She just put together one of the best scoring seasons in WNBA history, averaging 25 points while shooting 51.4% from the field and 45.2% from three.
And the Valkyries were undoubtedly going to be represented too; Veronica Burton has been the team’s most important player in my view (despite being their third-leading scorer), and as such, she was on my Second Team. While the Valkyries are a deep squad rather than a top-heavy one, I still felt compelled to have at least one player from the roster on the All-WNBA team.
I wanted a Washington Mystics representative as well, and ultimately concluded that Shakira Austin has been the team’s most critical player from top to bottom, although a strong case could be made for Sonia Citron, too. But Austin has been an elite rim protector and the team’s leading scorer, and she’s tied with Kiki Iriafen as the team’s leading rebounder.
I ultimately picked Jackie Young because she’s been one of the best No. 2 options in the WNBA; she’s averaging 19.3 points on high efficiency, and she’s on a third-seeded Aces squad.
And Angel Reese established herself as the Dream’s most impactful all-around player as the year progressed; she was my Defensive Player of the Year pick, she’s the best rebounder in the league, and she’s also averaging 16.4 points per game, which is the 18th-most in the WNBA.
It might just be time for a Third Team. Here are just a few players who were painful omissions from my All-WNBA ballot.
Aliyah Boston, Indiana Fever
Aliyah Boston is an All-WNBA-level player — and she’s been particularly crucial to the Fever defensively — but I couldn’t justify putting three Fever players on the All-WNBA team, especially when the Fever aren’t a Top 4 seed. And Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell were more consistent contributors this season.
Kayla McBride, Minnesota Lynx
If the Lynx were to have a second All-WNBA player, it’d be Kayla McBride, who had a phenomenal season on both ends of the floor. And a part of me really wanted to give the Lynx a second player, especially because the Aces and Fever got them with worse records.
Rhyne Howard, Atlanta Dream
Rhyne Howard has been pivotal to the Dream on both ends of the floor. But I only had room for one Dream player, and ultimately concluded Angel Reese’s impact on the glass and on the defensive end outweighed the fact that she wasn’t the team’s top-performing offensive player.
Allisha Gray, Atlanta Dream
Last year, Allisha Gray was a First Team player, and she hasn’t gotten worse. So, her omission this year is more of a result of the fact that the league got better (and healthier). Gray has been the Dream’s leading scorer, but Reese has been the more impactful all-around player.
Sonia Citron, Washington Mystics
Sonia Citron is one of the most impactful two-way guards in the game, and I considered her being the Mystics rep over Austin. Austin ultimately had a slight edge, but I wouldn’t be upset at any ballots that listed Citron.
Gabby Williams, Golden State Valkyries
Given the Valkyries’ dominance, I considered putting Gabby Williams on the Second Team alongside Burton. But it was hard to pick her over Young and Mitchell, who have had more impressive individual seasons on winning teams. Williams is an elite defender and is rewarded on my All-Defense First Team.
One thing I’ve learned in my two years as a WNBA awards voter: there’s no way to feel 100% about an awards ballot — and this ballot is no exception.

articles.title_orig: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order
articles.title_zh: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order
articles.content_orig:
CNN White House reporter Betsy Klein, seen here back at the White House on Thursday, was reportedly denied access earlier in the day
CNN, Politico and MS NOW are back in the White House, hours after a federal judge ruled President Donald Trump's ban on the three news outlets was probably unconstitutional and ordered their access immediately restored.
The outlets sought an emergency court hearing to regain entry accusing the White House in a court filing of having "repeatedly violated" the judge's ruling by turning away their journalists. The hearing was called off after access was restored.
Trump initially said he barred the outlets because of "fake news". The White House later cited national security.
But in his overnight ruling, Judge Timothy Kelly cast doubt on the claim about national security concerns.
The chaotic standoff limited some TV coverage as Trump welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House ahead of a state dinner later.
Judge Kelly ruled the ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".
CNN, Politico and MS Now all reported being denied entry to the White House on Thursday morning, prompting their request for an emergency hearing.
In response, the director of White House Operations said in a court filing that the press passes and confiscated badges had been restored by 09:45.
Shortly afterwards, all three outlets said they were allowed back in.
However, networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC, which pulled out in solidarity, have yet to confirm they will resume broadcast coverage from the White House.
Judge dismisses Trump lawsuit against Iowa newspaper and pollster over 2024 race
Judge Kelly ruled CNN, Politico and MS NOW were "likely to succeed" in showing the White House had not exercised "adequate due process" in the ban.
The judge also rejected the argument that national security concerns underpinned the exclusion, pointing out the president made no mention of this in his initial announcement.
"The record lacks factual support for defendants' contention that the revocation of plaintiffs' hard passes will in fact protect national security," Kelly wrote.
He ordered the immediate return of the outlets' press passes and a halt to enforcement of the ban for 14 days.
In a court filing on Tuesday, the US Department of Justice had accused the news outlets of threatening national security with their coverage.
Government lawyers cited stories about missile stockpiles, the construction of the White House ballroom and the recent Republican midterm convention.
What is the White House pool and why is it in a row with Trump?
Trump first announced last Friday he was barring CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
By Saturday morning, each outlet reported that they were denied entry to the White House grounds and that their press badges were confiscated.
All three outlets accused the Trump administration of violating their constitutional rights.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
And more than 50 media organisations across the ideological spectrum filed an amicus brief in support of the lawsuit, including Fox News, the New York Times, the Washington Post and the Wall Street Journal.
There have been previous instances of administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.
The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a specific press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.
But after objections from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was allowed in.

articles.content_orig:
FOX Weather Meteorologist Ian Oliver breaks down the latest updates on the incoming Nor'easter as states across the Mid-Atlantic region have already begun to endure intense winds, rain, and coastal flooding.
The East Coast is beginning to see the impacts of a developing nor'easter , with major coastal flooding from New Jersey to Virginia. All told, millions from New England to the Carolinas will experience days of coastal flooding, strong winds and pounding surf through the weekend.
The system that will become the first nor'easter of the season is set to emerge off the Mid-Atlantic coast between Thursday and Friday before charging towards the heavily populated Northeast .
TIMELINE: HERE'S WHERE AND WHEN MAJOR US CITIES WILL SEE IMPACTS FROM THE DEVELOPING NOR'EASTER
The increasing coastal flood risk will linger throughout the workweek from North Carolina 's Outer Banks to New England as strong northeasterly winds develop across the offshore and coastal waters, producing powerful wind gusts.
OUTER BANKS FIRST IN LINE FOR DEVELOPING NOR’EASTER AS DANGEROUS IMPACTS BEGIN WEDNESDAY
Seas will rise rapidly, creating heavy surf and dangerous, battering waves along exposed beaches .
Members of the North Carolina Department of Transportation work to establish natural coastal resilience along the beach.
According to the FOX Forecast Center , persistent onshore winds will remain locked in through multiple high tide cycles , allowing waves to relentlessly pound the base of coastal dunes.
Significant beach erosion and dune scarping will develop from the Outer Banks through the Mid-Atlantic and Long Island as the surface low-pressure system forms.
Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding during high tides has already started to impact especially low-lying coastal areas like Highway 12 in the North Carolina Outer Banks.
Sea rise could be anywhere from 2 to 3 feet, the FOX Forecast Center said.
FULL MOON COULD WORSEN NOR’EASTER FLOODING ALONG EAST COAST — HERE ARE 5 PLACES TO WATCH
Heading into Thursday, things shift as the surface low pressure system centralizes and strengthens off the Southeast coast and onshore winds expand and intensify.
Widespread tidal flooding will be possible as water becomes unable to drain during low tides and gets trapped in back bays and low-lying areas along the coast.
Early impacts of the developing Nor'easter in Ocean City, New Jersey, where coastal erosion has significantly affected the beach, as residents prepare for severe impacts from the storm throughout this week.
Some places could even see major flooding, with the FOX Forecast Center saying some of the worst flooding could happen in coastal Maryland and Virginia .
Rain and winds are also predicted to become an issue at this point, with wind gusts between 40 and 50 mph in some coastal areas, pushing ocean water inland.
NOR'EASTER LIVE TRACKER: FUTURE RADAR, WINDS, STORM SURGE, RAIN AND ALERTS
Days of these continuous pounding waves will severely impact beaches. Dune washouts, overwashes and damage to oceanfront boardwalks or coastal infrastructure are increasingly likely across Mid-Atlantic and Long Island beaches.
New England should start seeing rain at this stage, with a Level 1 out of 4 flood threat in effect for Boston , and parts of Rhode Island .
Beginning Saturday, the nor'easter really becomes prominent as the center of the low pressure system moves toward the Interstate 95 corridor and New England.
WILL THE MONSTER NOR'EASTER CANCEL YOUR WEEKEND PLANS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW
As the strengthening system tracks into or near New England, the strongest pressure gradient will impact the region, including Boston .
The exact track is still not certain, with some models pushing the low toward Boston, while others show the low pressure closer to New Jersey and Long Island, or even staying offshore. All three scenarios will create more significant impacts in different areas.
If the storm shifts closer to Boston, this could turn the storm into a major weather event, featuring 60 to 70 mph wind gusts, heavy rainfall , major storm surge and significant disruptions to Boston Harbor and the Massachusetts coastline, the FOX Forecast Center said.
If the storm shifts closer to New Jersey or Long Island, the strongest impacts could shift farther south, potentially putting New York City on the fringe of the storm.
Lashing winds and nasty weather are in store for thousands of residents along the coast of Nags Head, North Carolina, as the impacts from the incoming Nor'easter are expected all week long.
Lastly, if the area of low pressure remains offshore, coastal New England could still experience rough surf, elevated tides and breezy conditions, while the heaviest rain and strongest winds remain displaced to the south and east over open water. The FOX Forecast Center said this scenario is the least likely of the three.
THIS NOR’EASTER MAY FOLLOW THE SAME PATH AS SUPERSTORM SANDY, BUT IT’S NOTHING LIKE IT
The FOX Forecast Center said no matter what, winds could gust more than 60 mph as the peak of the storm shifts into southern New England, Massachusetts Bay and the Gulf of Maine .
Dangerous seas, extreme rip currents and massive swells will make ocean waters extremely dangerous.
Rain continues in New England through Sunday. A Level 1 out of 4 flash flood threat stretches from Cape Cod, Rhode Island and coastal Massachusetts, expanding north into parts of New Hampshire. Rain totals will be heaviest along coastal locations.
Impacts are expected to linger through Monday, but as the storm's track becomes more certain, the forecast could change slightly.
Stay with FOX Weather for the latest as we continue to track this developing storm.

articles.title_orig: Senate narrowly votes down resolution calling for end to Iran war
articles.title_zh: Senate narrowly votes down resolution calling for end to Iran war
articles.content_orig:
The Senate on Thursday narrowly voted down a measure demanding an end to the U.S. war with Iran .
The chamber voted 49-50 on the resolution, the latest to call for an end to the war.
All but four Republicans voted against the measure despite concerns that GOP candidates will face fallout in November's midterm elections from the war's economic costs. Some Republicans running in tight races have recently broken with President Donald Trump and called for an end to the war to bring gas prices down , a sign of potential voter discontent over the war's impact on the economy.
The Republicans who voted for the resolution were Sens. Thom Tillis of North Carolina, Maine's Susan Collins , Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky. Sen. John Fetterman of Pennsylvania was the lone Democrat to vote against it.
Sen. Angela Alsobrooks , D-Md., did not vote despite having been in the Senate earlier Thursday. Alsobrooks has previously voted for similar resolutions. But if she had again voted that way on Thursday, the resolution still would have failed.
"Senator Alsobrooks has voted 13 times to end the war in Iran. Unfortunately, she was dealing with an urgent family matter during today's vote so was unable to cast her fourteenth vote to end the war in Iran," Alsobrooks' spokesperson Meredith Happy said in a statement to CNBC. "She believes every day that this war rages on, Americans are paying for it at the gas pump and the grocery store—and too many American service members have paid with their lives. She continues to urge this President to end this war once and for all."
An affirmative vote on the measure, known as a War Powers Resolution , would have directed Trump to remove U.S. troops from hostilities in Iran unless Congress explicitly approves the war.
The Senate has voted repeatedly on similar measures since the war began, approving one of them. The White House has effectively ignored that vote, arguing that the War Powers Act is unconstitutional.
The measure voted on Thursday, which like the one adopted was a so-called "concurrent resolution," did not carry the force of law and is never signed by the president, making the vote largely symbolic even if it had passed.
The Democratic leaders of the legislative push, however, argue that the Constitution vests authority to declare war in Congress, not the executive branch, and that the president must abide by their disapproval whether or not he signs it.
"The president right now is in violation of the Constitution and the War Powers Act and the concurrent resolution that we've already passed," said Sen. Tim Kaine , D-Va., who has led a number of the votes to end the war.
"We shouldn't have to do a second one because the president should follow the law, but we are doing a second one on the theory that maybe after a number of months more people will join us, the American public is even more deeply opposed to this war."
The measure cleared the House in July and faced just a 50-vote threshold to clear the Senate. Democrats have seen an uptick in Republican support in recent votes to end the war, as the administration has blown through timelines to seek congressional approval for the conflict.
The war has also created a challenging political environment for incumbent Republicans, who could lose control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections that loom less than six weeks away.
Gas prices, which have spiked throughout the conflict, currently average $4.48 per gallon nationwide, according to AAA . Recently, runaway diesel prices have begun stressing farmers and truckers and have alarmed Republicans in midwestern states, who have begun to distance themselves from the White House and call for an end to the war.
Lawmakers are set to hit the campaign trail for nearly all of October, and will need to explain to voters what they are doing to bring down prices.
"There are a lot of good things we can talk about; the problem is what you did for me recently doesn't even hardly count," said Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., when asked about how Republicans can message to economically anxious voters. "The other thing that we get to talk about ... is that at least we're not socialists."

articles.content_orig:
NFL.com editors Jeremy Bergman , Brooke Cersosimo , Gennaro Filice , Bobby Kownack and Dan Parr will predict the winner of every game in the 2026 NFL season, using the unbeatable combo of football analysis and excessive punctuation. Check out their Week 3 NFL picks below.
Why Brooke picked the Packers: The Packers, lucky to eke out a victory in New York to avoid falling to 0-2, finally return to beloved Lambeau Field, where they have won each of their last 13 home openers. I have concerns about Jordan Love 's O-line, which just lost starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele for the season and has others banged up (OG Aaron Banks , OT Anthony Belton and backup OL Donovan Jennings ). Love has already taken seven sacks (tied for third-most), faced the fifth-highest pressure rate in the NFL this season (42.3%) and is tied for the most unblocked pressures faced (12), per NFL Pro . How Matt LaFleur game plans for his shorthanded offense against a Falcons defense that ranks first against the run, ninth on third down and in the red zone and has generated pressure on 41.5 percent on dropbacks (seventh in the NFL, per Next Gen Stats) could tell part of Thursday night's story. Not having CB A.J. Terrell hurts Atlanta's chances of slowing Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but having Michael Penix Jr. under center should be a boon for that team. Even if he's still knocking off the rust, this should look like a more competent unit, one that's better-suited to get Bijan Robinson , Drake London and Kyle Pitts more involved. These are two flawed teams, and though I think we'll see an improved Falcons outfit, Green Bay has a much-needed home-field edge and a defense that's playing with confidence with budding star Lukas Van Ness at the forefront. Clean up the penalties and this could be a turning point for the Pack.
Why Bobby picked the Bills: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. I will not be picking the Chargers for a third straight week -- nor am I likely to throw my support behind them very much at all in the coming months, considering the juggernauts lined up to face them . First up on that list: the Bills, who look to be the cream of the AFC crop in the early goings of this season. Josh Allen is on fire, having already accounted for nine touchdowns (five passing, four rushing) while leading Buffalo to 36 or more points in each of the team’s first two games. While there are some pressing questions about the Bills' defense, nothing has come easy to the Chargers in Mike McDaniel’s new scheme. Justin Herbert looks uncomfortable, his pass catchers have been affected by multiple big drops and injuries, and lead back Omarion Hampton has lost a fumble in both games. There’s nothing to suggest Los Angeles can string together enough scoring drives to keep up with Buffalo’s mighty offense. Look for the Bills to move to 3-0 in dominating fashion.
Why Bobby picked the Panthers: Cleveland’s upset victory over the Buccaneers felt more like Tampa Bay continuing to be the team that fell on its face throughout the end of last season than a sign the Browns will stick it to another NFC South opponent. Lest that be misconstrued as a “ Browns is the Browns ” take, Cleveland played well and fought hard for its win. Deshaun Watson was as precise as he’s been in years, rookie Denzel Boston looks like a stud, and the Browns defense was the far more composed side during the game’s final two minutes in the aftermath of a 132-minute weather delay. The Panthers just happen to be playing better ball than both the Bucs and the Browns. Bryce Young is off to the best start of his career, buoyed by the budding wide receiver duo of Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker . He’s averaged 324 passing yards through two games with three touchdown passes in each contest. It’s not out of the question he keeps it going against a Cleveland defense still navigating the early days of the post- Myles Garrett era. The wild card remains the Panthers’ defensive Jekyll-and-Hyde act to start the season. Are they the closer to the group that gave up 59 points to an explosive Bears team in the opener or the unit that dominated a woeful Falcons squad while allowing just 3 points ? Even if it’s more the former, Dave Canales’ offense should be able to do enough for a victory.
Why Jeremy picked the Lions: Aaron Glenn's return to Detroit, where he was Dan Campbell's defensive coordinator for four seasons, will be the ultimate test for his Jets defense's early turnaround. After games against the Titans and Packers offenses (asterisk needed), Gang Green's defense, which received an influx of veteran talent in the offseason, ranks in the top three in yards per game (197.0, first), yards per play (4.0, third) and third-down conversion rate (23.8, second). New York will be without a few injured vets in the Motor City but should get back Joseph Ossai for Sunday's game. Whether Glenn's Jets feast depends on which Lions team shows up. Detroit has a talent advantage on offense but has yet to play a complete game this season (nearly blowing Week 1 against New Orleans, forgetting to show up until the second half of the Bills loss). The Lions defense is banged up, but so is New York's receiving corps. Detroit's best bet Sunday is getting to Geno Smith with Aidan Hutchinson and Co.; the QB hasn't turned the ball over yet, but he's faced a 43.4% pressure rate, second in the NFL only to the injured Jayden Daniels , and the veteran is due despite his claims otherwise . As Week 2 proved, the Jets still need to learn how to win. New York is close, but the lesson won't come this week against a tested Lions team.
Why Gennaro picked the Texans: Is this an elimination game in September? As the only Week 3 matchup between winless teams, this AFC South showdown screams desperation. Since 1990, just 2.9 percent of squads that lost their first three games went on to make the playoffs. We’re talkin’ five out of 171, people. Of course, last year’s Texans were one of those five. And while Houston’s hyped defense looked shockingly porous against Josh Allen ’s Bills in Week 1, the unit largely stifled Joe Burrow and the Bengals last Sunday. I anticipate continued success against a one-dimensional Colts offense. Jonathan Taylor ’s a stud, no doubt, but he has to be a one-man army with Daniel Jones still seemingly working his way back from last December’s Achilles tear. Add in the fact that Indianapolis' $114 million field stretcher just hit injured reserve , and Houston can commit additional resources to stopping the Colts' bell-cow back. Meanwhile, Indy's defense hasn’t been able to stop anyone , giving up the second-most yards EVER in the first two weeks of a season:
1) 2016 Raiders: 1,035 yards allowed 2) 2026 Colts: 1,029 T-3) 1967 Falcons: 1,025 T-3) 2017 Saints: 1,025
Oddly enough, the two bookends on that list -- the 2016 Raiders and 2017 Saints -- both made the playoffs with double-digit wins. Maybe the Colts have everyone right where they want them! … Or maybe they’re doomed to suffer a sixth straight loss to C.J. Stroud and Co.
Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue preview the Week 3 matchup between the Texans and the Colts.
Why Dan picked the Jaguars: There will be no sneaking up on anyone for this season’s Jaguars and Patriots, not after they both surprised in 2025. Sunday’s meeting is an opportunity to establish which squad has more staying power in the AFC’s upper ranks, and the trenches might dictate which team has the edge. Jacksonville needs better play from the offensive line, especially on the interior, if it’s going to bounce back from blowing a lead against Denver. New England has a duo that can exploit a team’s weakness up the middle, with Milton Williams and Christian Barmore at defensive tackle. One thing that could work in the Jags’ favor is the Pats' ailing health. New England has taken hits to the league’s No. 1 scoring defense -- edge rusher Dre’Mont Jones and safety Craig Woodson missed Wednesday’s practice

articles.title_orig: Melania Trump hosts China's first lady for an outing that is watched for diplomacy and style - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Melania Trump hosts China's first lady for an outing that is watched for diplomacy and style - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
First ladies Melania Trump and Peng Liyuan are touring the Smithsonian's National Museum of Asian Art, celebrating cultural ties between the United States and China during China’s diplomatic visit to Washington
WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — Melania Trump and Peng Liyuan on Thursday toured one of the largest Asian art museums in the United States, celebrating cultural ties between the U.S. and China during a high-profile diplomatic visit to Washington.
Leaving their husbands behind at the White House, the first ladies visited the Smithsonian's National Museum of Asian Art in a display of soft power that united two figures known for fusing style and diplomacy . It was the first public meeting in nearly a decade between the spouses, one a former fashion model and the other a famed soprano.
Crowds had gathered on the sidewalk across from the museum, many waving Chinese and American flags. The groups also held long banners with Chinese text.
Inside the museum, the first ladies visited the Peacock Room, a gilded green, blue and gold dining room that was once housed in a London mansion before opening to the public in Washington in 1923. The room was created by American artist James McNeill Whistler.
They also saw the “Princess from the Land of Porcelain,” an oil painting by Whistler hanging in the room and featuring a kimono-clad woman standing and holding a fan.
The meeting had the potential to become a global spectacle, featuring two powerful and glamorous women from the world's two biggest economies.
“They definitely add to the grandiosity and the symbolic significance of this trip,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center, a Washington think tank.
Every interaction between the first ladies will be scrutinized for clues about the standing between their countries, Sun said. Just as likely to draw attention are their style choices, which are closely observed in fashion circles and are frequent fodder for social media.
“In terms of presentation, these two first ladies are going to be impeccable,” Sun said, adding that both are trained as “professional presenters.”
Their last public meeting was in 2017, when President Donald Trump stopped in Beijing during a tour of Asia in his first term. During that trip, the first ladies shared tea at the Palace Museum and visited a school where students performed songs and dances. Melania Trump did not attend her husband’s visit to Beijing earlier this year.
Peng has embraced a more public role than her predecessors, who rarely attended state visits and usually stayed in the background. Melania Trump keeps a lower profile, often preferring to work behind the scenes.
They split off from the White House on Thursday while Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held private talks , touring the museum after a White House welcome ceremony and before a lavish state dinner.
Peng’s last trip to the White House was in 2015, when President Barack Obama hosted Xi. A noted star before her husband's rise, Peng ascended to national fame in the 1980s as a military singer, performing patriotic songs in full dress uniform.
She is also a public welfare advocate, taking on roles that have little precedent for her position in China. She has been an official antismoking ambassador in China, and in 2011 she was appointed as the World Health Organization goodwill ambassador for tuberculosis and HIV/AIDS.
Peng has been appearing more in public recently following a period in which she was less visible on the global stage because of the COVID-19 pandemic and a cutback in diplomatic trips by her husband.
The Smithsonian's Asian art museum is one of the largest of its kind in the United States. It also has been a target of the Trump administration’s attempt to eliminate what it sees as liberal ideology from the institution's museums.
The White House last year ordered a review of Smithsonian museums to make sure exhibits “celebrate American exceptionalism” and “remove divisive or partisan narratives.”
The museum, located along the National Mall, features more than 46,000 objects dating from the Neolithic period to the present, according to its website. It has been part of a broader Smithsonian effort to return stolen or unethically obtained objects to their home countries. Last year, the museum returned fragments of a silk manuscript from China that dated to more than 2,000 years ago and had been looted from a tomb.
In a Fox News Channel interview on Wednesday, Melania Trump said she was taking Peng to the museum to show the “connection with the culture, with us and China.”
When Peng visited the White House in 2015, she joined first lady Michelle Obama at a naming ceremony for a giant panda at the National Zoo. The ceremony also featured songs sung by preschoolers at a local Chinese immersion school. The panda, Bei Bei , was later returned to China in 2019 to enter a breeding program.
Associated Press writers Didi Tang and Fu Ting contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Atlanta junior among 2 Ole Miss students found dead in Mississippi
articles.title_zh: Atlanta junior among 2 Ole Miss students found dead in Mississippi
articles.content_orig:
ATLANTA — The family of a metro Atlanta college student found dead at the University of Mississippi is speaking out for the first time as investigators work to determine what led to his death.
Robert Strang, a 20-year-old junior at Ole Miss and graduate of North Atlanta High School, was found dead Monday. Another student, 18-year-old Aidan Hamilton, was also found dead the same day at a separate location.
Authorities have not said whether the two deaths are connected, and both investigations remain ongoing.
Parents outside North Atlanta High School told Channel 2’s Tom Regan they were saddened to learn of Strang’s death.
“It’s heartbreaking that someone has lost their son,” one parent said.
Students at Ole Miss are also struggling to process the loss.
“We didn’t think to come back to such sad news of losing two classmates,” said student Raven Tunstall. “College is supposed to be where we grow and gain new experiences. It’s not supposed to be where our lives end.”
Investigators are now focusing on whether kratom, a controversial herbal supplement, may have played a role in either death.
Authorities said a package of retail kratom purchased from a convenience store was found at both scenes.
Kratom is a plant-based substance that is sold in some convenience stores, smoke shops and gas stations.
Critics have raised concerns about its potential health risks, particularly with concentrated or synthetic products.
The substance has been banned by some state and local governments, including the city of Oxford, Mississippi, where Ole Miss is located.
“It makes me concerned because I know kids can get kratom at gas stations, and I don’t think they are aware of the dangers,” one parent said.
As questions remain about how Strang died, his family released a statement expressing their grief.
“We are heartbroken by the loss of our son Robert and are trying to process this unimaginable loss,” the family said. “We are deeply grateful for the outpouring of love, prayers and support by so many beloved friends and family. Their kindness has meant more to our family than we can ever express.”
Investigators say toxicology tests will be critical in determining whether kratom was a contributing factor in either student’s death.
Those results are expected to take several weeks.

articles.title_orig: Ukrainian man kills one, wounds four in Poland abbey knife attack
articles.title_zh: Ukrainian man kills one, wounds four in Poland abbey knife attack
articles.content_orig:
One person was killed and four others injured when a man armed with a knife attacked clergy and worshippers at a Catholic monastery in southern Poland.
Police said the 31-year-old attacker, a Ukrainian national, went on a stabbing spree at the 17th-century Benedictine abbey in Jaroslaw, some 30km (19 miles) from the border with Ukraine, on Thursday morning.
The suspect, who had entered Poland from Germany earlier in the day, reportedly grabbed a knife from the abbey’s kitchen and attacked four men and one woman, including a priest in a confessional, police said.
“Three of the victims are clergy members and two are laypeople; one person has died,” said prosecutor Bozena Harasz-Wołoszyn. Two others were in “critical, life-threatening condition”.
Polish media identified the man who died as a priest. Police did not immediately confirm the identity of the deceased.
Prosecutors said the attacker was headed for a nearby border crossing back into Ukraine but instead went to the abbey.
The motive remains unclear, and doctors will assess whether he was under the influence of alcohol, Harasz-Wołoszyn said.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the “murderer” would be “punished with the full severity of Polish law”.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack a “horrific crime”.
“The perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility in accordance with the law … We are shaken by this evil. Justice must be done.”
The mayor of Jaroslaw, Marcin Nazarewicz, declared a period of mourning until the end of the week.
Stabbings, particularly at religious sites, are extremely rare in Poland, one of Europe’s most Catholic countries.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’
articles.content_orig:
Israeli PM attacks critics and calls New York mayor Zohran Mamdani ‘antisemitic’ in inflammatory address
Benjamin Netanyahu delivered an inflammatory address to the United Nations on Thursday, decrying what he said was a global anti-Jewish conspiracy and swatting aside criticism of Israel’s war in Gaza, as he faces down international isolation and a fight for political survival in upcoming elections in Israel.
As planned protests erupted on the streets of New York City, Netanyahu took aim at critics of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the international media, regional leaders such as Turkey’s Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the leftwing commentator Hasan Piker and the New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani in an address that doubled as a stump speech to ignite his rightwing base for the elections.
Invoking his late brother Yonatan Netanyahu, a commando killed in a 1976 raid to free Israeli hostages from a hijacked airliner in Entebbe, Uganda, he repeated the lines: “We are going to win. We have no other choice.”
Dozens of delegates, inspired by a Palestinian call, walked out of the General Assembly Hall of the UN headquarters as Netanyahu took the stage, leading a speaker to pound his gavel and announce: “I’m calling for order in the hall.”
Palestinian representatives organising diplomatic missions to bring staff for a planned walkout of Netanyahu’s speech said they wanted to “send a clear message to Netanyahu and his government that no one is willing to aid, abet, or be complicit in its genocide and war crimes and illegal occupation, which all peace-loving states and peoples demand must come to an end”.
“If there are any other moral cowards in the audience, I urge them to walk out,” Netanyahu said before launching into his prepared remarks.
The speech revealed little new in terms of Israeli policy over the war in Gaza , militant settler violence in the West Bank, or Israel’s plans to end other regional conflicts including its joint war with the United States against Iran.
But he argued that the world faced an existential threat from Iran, suggesting that several missiles from Tehran could have destroyed the UN, and cited quiet support from world leaders for Israel’s actions that could not be aired in public.
“Devastating Iran’s nuclear facilities was … very hard to do,” he said of launching joint US-Israeli strikes in February. “But for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make as prime minister. Because if we hadn’t done it, we’d all be dead.”
He branded Turkey’s Erdoğan as a “tyrant” who “hosts Hamas terrorists”, decried Mamdani as the “antisemitic mayor of New York”, and declared that Israel’s war in Gaza is not genocide – “it’s the opposite of genocide”.
“So, to all those spreading these lies about my country and about our brave soldiers, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the antisemitic mayor of New York, I say this: shame on you!” he said.
Netanyahu delivered the controversial address to the United Nations on Thursday just hours after Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas said his delegation was “unlawfully” denied visas by the Trump administration to attend the meeting of world leaders.
In a video address from Ramallah, broadcast in the General Assembly Hall, Abbas condemned Israel’s policies in Gaza, the West Bank and East Jerusalem as a “malicious colonial plan” to establish a “‘Greater Israel’ and erase the Palestinian presence”.
Citing the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and the violent expansion of settlements in the West Bank, Abbas said that the Israeli government “now threatens the very life and existence of the Palestinian people in their homeland”.
“Do not allow another Nakba and further massacres like those of 1948 to continue taking place,” he added, referring to the expulsion of Palestinians upon the founding of Israel.
For the second year in a row, the US state department denied visas to Abbas and the Palestinian Authority delegation, arguing that they had failed to live up to their commitments to seek peace with Israel.
“As a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace, the United States will extend sanctions that deny visas to PLO members and PA officials,” the state department said last week in a statement.
In his speech, Abbas said his delegation “[rejects] these unlawful punitive measures, as well as the accusations and justifications on which they were based”.
He said: “Preventing the Palestinian delegation from reaching United Nations headquarters is inconsistent with the obligations of the United States as the host country.”
As he spoke, protests were forming on the streets of New York near the United Nations headquarters in advance of Netanyahu’s arrival.
Hundreds of demonstrators crowded into the street on Manhattan’s east side in midtown and held signs that said “End the Genocide” and wore shirts reading “Fund people not bombs”. By the end of Netanyahu’s speech, more than 100 demonstrators, including several local elected officials, had been arrested by New York City police.
Earlier this summer, the mayor, Zohran Mamdani, had said that Netanyahu was “not welcome” in New York, and said he was reviewing whether Netanyahu could be arrested by city police under an international criminal court warrant for his arrest.
He has since tempered that stance, saying this week that he wouldn’t attend the protests but promising to protect their “right to [protest] in this city”.
Netanyahu is not expected to meet Donald Trump, who is in Washington to host the Chinese leader, Xi Jinping, nor with other senior US officials, as he faces growing international condemnation over his hardline stance. Netanyahu has said that he needs to return to Israel quickly because of the election campaign and the holiday of Sukkot, which begins on Friday.

articles.title_orig: China's Xi says they will send 2 giant pandas to Zoo Atlanta, calling them "envoy of friendship"
articles.title_zh: China's Xi says they will send 2 giant pandas to Zoo Atlanta, calling them "envoy of friendship"
articles.content_orig:
Chinese President Xi Jinping announced some panda diplomacy on Thursday during a meeting with President Trump and other White House officials, saying that two pandas are an "envoy of friendship."
The short announcement was the latest update since the Atlanta zoo announced a new research agreement with the China Wildlife Conservation Association. As part of that agreement, the organization expects to send over male panda Ping Ping and female panda Fu Shuang, from the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding.
Xi said Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, "will come to their new home in Zoo Atlanta and meet with the American people" in "a few days." He called it "a piece of good news" and hailed the panda loan program as an example of "friendship between the Chinese and Americans."
"We can't wait to meet Ping Ping and Fu Shuang and to welcome our members, guests, city, and community back to the wonder and joy of giant pandas," the zoo's president, Raymond B. King, said in a statement in April.
China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said that the new round of cooperation on conservation would help improve the health and well-being of the giant pandas, advance global biodiversity protection and strengthen the friendship between the Chinese and American people.
During an earlier giant panda agreement between the zoo and China that concluded in 2024, pandas Lun Lun and Yang Yang gave birth to seven bears, the zoo said. Lun Lun and Yang Yang and their two youngest offspring left Atlanta for China in October 2024, where the rest of their offspring reside.
Details about when Ping Ping and Fu Shuang may arrive in Atlanta remain limited. A spokesperson for the zoo told CBS News Atlanta that they would not be sharing the date at this time. In the meantime, zoo officials say they were carrying out facility upgrades, among other preparation work, to create a more comfortable and safer environment for the pair with technical guidance from Chinese experts.
Giant pandas have been a symbol of the U.S.-China friendship ever since Beijing gifted a pair of pandas to the National Zoo in Washington, D.C. in 1972, and China has long used its giant panda loan program as a tool of Beijing's soft power diplomacy worldwide.
Currently, two zoos in the United States have pandas. The National Zoo and the San Diego Zoo both received pandas from China in 2024.
The Associated  Press contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: California sheriff broke election law by seizing ballots, state Supreme Court rules
articles.title_zh: California sheriff broke election law by seizing ballots, state Supreme Court rules
articles.content_orig:
State supreme court rules Chad Bianco’s conduct unlawful and says he ‘must refrain from further handling’ of ballots
A Republican California sheriff must return more than a half-million ballots he seized for an investigation into unfounded voting improprieties in a special election last year, the state supreme court ruled Thursday.
Riverside county sheriff Chad Bianco in February seized approximately 650,000 ballots from a November 2025 special election on statewide congressional redistricting favorable to Democrats and pushed by Governor Gavin Newsom. The measure easily passed statewide, and won in Bianco’s county by roughly 80,000 votes.
The court called the ballots’ seizure “unlawful”, saying California law requires voted ballots to remain in the custody and control of election officials, even during a criminal investigation. Bianco must also “refrain from further handling of the ballots except as necessary to comply with our order”, the court said in an unanimous decision. Bianco did not immediately comment on the ruling.
“Today’s ruling affirms that in California we will defend democracy – using every branch of government,” Newsom said in a statement. “People deserve to know their ballot is counted and secure, and in California we will do everything we can to protect that constitutional right – this year, and beyond.”
Newsom on Saturday signed a bill that would prevent anyone from seizing ballots, as Bianco did.
“The new laws I signed just last week add new protections so attacks like this cannot happen again,” Newsom said on Thursday.
Bianco’s ballot investigation came as Donald Trump has repeatedly disputed the results of the 2020 election, citing unsubstantiated instances of fraud. His administration in January seized ballots and other documents from an election office in Georgia. Some Republicans have mirrored Trump’s rhetoric on voting in their states. Election officials and civil rights groups have been following the Bianco case carefully as they brace for the possibility that Trump or his allies may try to seize ballots in November.
Bianco said he confiscated the election materials as part of a criminal investigation after receiving a complaint from a local citizens group that the count was off. Local election officials had previously said the complaint was unfounded. Bianco, was running for governor at the time, but he did not make it through the primary.
Democratic attorney general Rob Bonta immediately launched a legal challenge, arguing Bianco had no authority over election materials and warning the seizure was designed to sow distrust in elections. He ordered Bianco to return the ballots, but Bianco did not.
The University of California, Los Angeles Voting Rights Project also sued the sheriff and the Riverside county registrar of voters on behalf of several Riverside county voters.

A U.S. citizen was left bloody and hospitalized after federal immigration enforcement agents mistook him for a fugitive, pinned him to the ground, and attempted to handcuff him in Evanston, Illinois , according to local police and eyewitnesses.
The encounter unfolded Sunday morning in the Chicago suburb when five agents in separate vehicles targeted the unidentified Black man, believing he matched the description of a fugitive with a Chicago arrest warrant. According to an Evanston Police Department news release, when the man refused to present identification, agents attempted to forcefully handcuff him.
Witnesses reported seeing agents pinning the man to the sidewalk while he repeatedly screamed that he was a U.S. citizen. Ryan Garton, a bystander who recorded video of the incident, told reporters that an agent had a knee on the man’s back. After agents realized the man was a citizen and not the suspect they were seeking, they left the scene.
Garton and local store owner Michael Lipson assisted the injured man until an ambulance arrived. Eyewitnesses described seeing bloodstains on the man's shirt, severe swelling around his eye, and facial scrapes. The victim told police his head, neck, and teeth were injured during the struggle.
Responding Evanston police officers noted that one federal agent also had blood on his hands. The agent told officers he sustained injuries during the scuffle and claimed the agents left the area immediately due to fears that gathering bystanders might attack them. Police visited the victim at St. Francis Hospital to document his injuries and have launched an investigation. Evanston Mayor Daniel Biss confirmed the man was treated for minor injuries, writing on social media that the city would "remain vigilant about federal activities."
The Department of Homeland Security defended the officers' actions in a statement, saying agents encountered an individual who "resembled the target" of an operation and that the man was "not cooperative and refused to identify himself." DHS claimed the officers left after the man identified himself and that he refused their offer of assistance.
The bloody altercation drew swift condemnation from local and state officials, including Illinois Rep. Jan Schakowsky, who stated she was "disgusted and outraged" by the reports.
The incident comes amid heightened scrutiny of federal immigration tactics, following a series of recent high-profile shootings and fatal encounters involving agents across the country.

Google Photos is rolling out a handful of new features, including a Redact Markup tool and “Moods” on Android.
The upgraded Markup tool adds three features, starting with a Redact pen that lets you blur/pixelate sensitive info in screenshots and images. There are also precise thickness sliders for the Pen and new fonts in the Text tool. This is rolling out globally to Google Photos for Android.
Moods let you easily apply a “nostalgic, vintage-inspired look” to pictures, including Crisp 35mm (film), 2000’s night (digicam), Retro contrast, Night light, Blue Haze, Any Minimalist, and Rich textures. You get slider controls, with each mood “intelligently adapt[ing] to your images.” This is rolling out globally on Android.
There are also 15 new Remix templates, including red carpet moments, whimsical birthday cards, and photo booth shots. This is rolling out in select countries on Android and iOS.
Google Photos is also highlighting how the Wardrobe feature is now available in Brazil, India, and the US on Android and iOS. An AI Pro or AI Ultra subscription is required. There’s also the Photos integration in Gemini Spark announced earlier this month.
